# JIRA API Tool Documentation

## Overview
This tool automatically adds code analysis reports to JIRA tickets as comments, providing seamless integration between git commits and project management.

## Features
- ✅ Automated JIRA comment posting with structured format
- ✅ Automatic ticket status updates based on change type
- ✅ Smart labeling for better categorization
- ✅ Commit hash linking to repository
- ✅ Secure API key management
- ✅ Configurable settings and defaults

## Setup

### 1. Configuration Setup
```powershell
# Copy the template configuration
Copy-Item .\.github\config\jira-config.template.json .\.github\config\jira-config.json

# Edit the configuration file with your credentials
notepad .\.github\config\jira-config.json
```

### 2. JIRA API Token Generation
1. Go to your JIRA account: https://id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens
2. Click "Create API token"
3. Give it a label (e.g., "Auto-Commit Tool")
4. Copy the generated token
5. Add it to your `jira-config.json` file

### 3. Configuration Parameters
```json
{
  "jiraUrl": "https://company.atlassian.net",           // Your JIRA instance URL
  "username": "your-email@company.com",                 // Your JIRA email
  "apiToken": "your-api-token-here",                    // Generated API token
  "autoStatusUpdate": true,                             // Auto-update ticket status
  "defaultStatus": "Code Review",                       // Default status for updates
  "autoLabels": true,                                   // Auto-add labels
  "defaultLabels": ["automated-commit"],                // Default labels to add
  "repositoryUrl": "https://github.com/org/repo",       // For commit links
  "settings": {
    "addTimestamp": true,                               // Include timestamps
    "includeCommitLink": true,                          // Link to commit
    "notifyAssignee": false                             // Notify ticket assignee
  }
}
```

## Usage

### Basic Usage
```powershell
.\.github\tools\jira-api.ps1 `
  -TicketNumber "RECO-12345" `
  -RootCause "Authentication service was missing proper error handling for invalid tokens" `
  -Solution "Added comprehensive error handling with user-friendly messages and proper logging" `
  -TestingRecommendations "Test invalid token scenarios, expired tokens, and malformed requests" `
  -CommitHash "abc123def456" `
  -FilesChanged "AuthService.cs, LoginController.cs, ErrorMessages.resx" `
  -LinesModified "+67 -23"
```

### Integrated with Git Workflow
```powershell
# After committing changes
$commitHash = git rev-parse HEAD
$filesChanged = (git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD) -join ", "
$stats = git diff --shortstat HEAD~1 HEAD

.\.github\tools\jira-api.ps1 `
  -TicketNumber "RECO-12345" `
  -RootCause "Issue description..." `
  -Solution "Solution approach..." `
  -TestingRecommendations "Testing guidance..." `
  -CommitHash $commitHash `
  -FilesChanged $filesChanged `
  -LinesModified $stats
```

### Custom Configuration Path
```powershell
.\.github\tools\jira-api.ps1 `
  -TicketNumber "RECO-12345" `
  # ... other parameters ...
  -ConfigPath "custom\path\to\config.json"
```

## Generated Comment Format
The tool generates JIRA comments in this format:

```
### Code Analysis Report - 2025-11-10 14:30:15

**Root Cause:**
Authentication service was missing proper error handling for invalid tokens

**Solution:**
Added comprehensive error handling with user-friendly messages and proper logging

**Testing Recommendations:**
Test invalid token scenarios, expired tokens, and malformed requests

**Commit Details:**
- Commit Hash: [abc123def456](https://github.com/your-repo/commit/abc123def456)
- Files Changed: AuthService.cs, LoginController.cs, ErrorMessages.resx
- Lines Modified: +67 -23

---
_Auto-generated by JIRA Auto-Commit Workflow_
```

## Error Handling
- **Missing Configuration**: Tool will guide you to create the config file
- **Invalid Credentials**: Clear error messages for authentication issues
- **Network Issues**: Retry logic and detailed error reporting
- **Invalid Ticket**: Validation of ticket number format and existence

## Security Notes
- ⚠️ **Never commit `jira-config.json` to version control**
- ✅ The `.gitignore` file is automatically configured to exclude it
- ✅ API tokens are more secure than passwords
- ✅ Consider using environment variables for CI/CD pipelines

## Troubleshooting

### Common Issues
1. **"Configuration file not found"**
   - Copy the template: `Copy-Item .\.github\config\jira-config.template.json .\.github\config\jira-config.json`
   - Edit with your credentials

2. **"Authentication failed"**
   - Verify your email and API token
   - Ensure the JIRA URL is correct
   - Check if your account has permission to comment on tickets

3. **"Ticket not found"**
  - Verify the ticket number format (e.g., "RECO-12345")
  - Ensure you have access to the project
  - Check if the ticket exists

4. **"Status update failed"**
   - Verify the status name exists in your workflow
   - Check if you have permission to transition tickets
   - Some statuses may require specific fields

## Advanced Features

### Custom Status Mapping
Edit your config to map change types to specific statuses:
```json
{
  "statusMapping": {
    "bug": "In Testing",
    "feature": "Code Review",
    "docs": "Done",
    "refactor": "Code Review"
  }
}
```

### Environment Variables
For CI/CD, you can use environment variables:
```powershell
$env:JIRA_API_TOKEN = "your-token"
# Tool will automatically use environment variables if config is missing
```

## Integration with VS Code
The tool is designed to work seamlessly with the JIRA auto-commit chatmode in VS Code, providing a complete workflow from code changes to JIRA updates.
